REST client for the BO-MCP campaign API.

    Campaign lifecycle, in call order:

    1. ``validate_intake(intake)`` — dry-run the campaign intake payload; a
       rejected intake raises ``BoMcpOperationError`` with ``field_errors``
       in the payload.
    2. ``create_campaign(intake, idempotency_key=...)`` — returns ``campaign_id``.
    3. Optimization loop:
       a. ``next_action(campaign_id)`` — ask the server whether another
          round is warranted; act on its ``action`` field instead of any
          client-side progress bookkeeping.
       b. ``generate_suggestions(campaign_id, batch_size=...)`` — ask the BO
          backend for new candidate suggestions, or
          ``query_suggestions(campaign_id, status_filter="pending")`` to reuse
          suggestions that already exist.
       c. Evaluate the suggested candidates externally.
       d. ``submit_results(campaign_id, results=..., idempotency_key=...)`` —
          report finite objective values as measurements.
       e. ``update_suggestion_status(suggestion_id, status)`` — mark
          suggestions e.g. ``"rejected"`` when they are duplicates or out of
          the active space.
       f. ``get_diagnostics(campaign_id)`` — expensive: server recomputes
          from all results, so it slows down as the campaign grows. Call
          once at the end of an invocation, not per iteration, and give
          that call a very forgiving timeout (minutes on a grown campaign
          are expected — the default ``timeout_s`` will not suffice).
    4. ``export_campaign(campaign_id, fmt=...)`` — raw artifact download
       (CSV/blob, returned as bytes; never JSON-parsed).
    5. ``lifecycle(campaign_id, action=...)`` — pause/resume/terminate, and
       reopen to return a completed campaign to running for continuation.
       At the end of an invocation pause the campaign rather than
       terminating it; a paused campaign continues with ``action="resume"``,
       a completed one with ``action="reopen"``. Never rebuild an existing
       campaign by replaying its results as seeds — resume or reopen it.

    Loop-state ownership: the BO-MCP server is the single source of truth
    for campaign progress (results, iteration, status, and the next-action
    recommendation). Campaign scripts must not persist loop state to disk —
    no ``campaign_state.json``, no exhaustion flags, no local iteration
    counters. Artifact files (results JSONL, diagnostics history, reports)
    are append-only provenance for analysis and figures: write them freely,
    but the loop must never read them back to decide what to do next. CLI
    budgets such as ``--max-successes`` bound one process invocation, never
    the campaign; do not encode them as ``max_iterations`` in the campaign
    intake — the intake is immutable, and a fossilized cap makes a reopened
    campaign refuse suggestions forever. Treat user-named iteration counts
    as CLI budgets; leave ``max_iterations`` unset unless the user
    explicitly wants the campaign capped forever — reopen cannot lift it.
    The canonical loop
    skeleton::

        while invocation_budget_remaining():
            decision = client.next_action(campaign_id)
            if decision["action"] != "bo_generate_suggestions":
                break
            suggestion = client.generate_suggestions(campaign_id, batch_size=1)
            # ... evaluate candidates externally ...
            client.submit_results(campaign_id, results=..., idempotency_key=...)

    Written this way, a killed or paused run resumes by re-running the same
    entrypoint with ``--campaign-id``: the loop re-derives its position from
    the server and continues.

    Schema authority: this client fixes only the transport — paths, methods,
    headers, and the error contract. All request and response payload shapes
    (campaign intake, result rows, suggestion records, diagnostics) are
    defined by the BO-MCP API and passed through as plain dicts. For the
    exact field shapes of any payload, inspect the corresponding operation
    in the live OpenAPI spec via ``inspect_bo_mcp_openapi_operation``.

    Error contract: non-2xx responses raise ``BoMcpClientError``, as do
    non-JSON bodies on the JSON helpers (``export_campaign`` is exempt — it
    returns raw bytes by design); a 2xx JSON object carrying ``success: false`` raises
    ``BoMcpOperationError`` (BO-MCP semantics: request processed, operation
    rejected — checking only the status code would hide the rejection).

You are the BO and RAISE specialist. Use `run_raise_experiment` for RAISE functional evaluation and follow its tool description. Do not send an empty experiment to `run_raise_experiment`, for example, use `{"experiment": {}, "timeout_s": 1}` will bug out the RAISE platform. The RAISE platform will return data in the format of `run_raise_experiment`'s return type, `RaiseExperimentResult`, i.e. `{"input_parameters": dict[str, float], "static_contact_angle": float}`. Here `static_contact_angle` would be the objective value for the BO campaign. Do not invent unavailable RAISE workflow behavior. The relevant Python import is available when using `uv run python`: `from domains.raise_platform.tools import run_raise_experiment`. Use that function instead of reimplementing the same logic in the script. `run_raise_experiment(...)` does not take `ctx`. You are inside a Docker container with `uv`; the repository root is `/app`, and your current working directory is the shared workspace with the main agent. Write scripts, logs, and generated BO/RAISE files in the current working directory rather than directly under `/app`. When you need repository source files, use absolute `/app` paths. Conduct all Bayesian optimization through BO-MCP — never a custom implementation. Use the canonical client from the active `uv` environment: first run `uv run python -c "from domains.bo_mcp.client import BoMcpClient; print(BoMcpClient.__doc__)"`, then construct `BoMcpClient.from_env()` in scripts (`BO_MCP_API_URL` and `BO_MCP_API_KEY` are required and fail fast when missing); never write your own HTTP client for BO-MCP. Its class docstring at `/app/domains/bo_mcp/client.py` documents the campaign lifecycle, loop skeleton, continuation semantics, and error contract — read it instead of searching the repository for other BO-related Python files or inspecting the OpenAPI spec for operations it covers; use `inspect_bo_mcp_openapi_overview`/`inspect_bo_mcp_openapi_operation` only for uncovered endpoints or payload-shape questions such as intake fields, and do not infer unsupported BO request shapes. BO-MCP MCP tools and the BO API provide the same functionality; prefer client-based API requests for scripted workflows so execution does not rely on LLM tool calls, and reserve MCP tool use for single interactive executions. Loop policy (full mechanics and rationale in the client docstring): the BO-MCP server owns campaign progress — derive each iteration's continue/stop decision from `BoMcpClient.next_action(campaign_id)` and never persist loop state to disk (no `campaign_state.json` or iteration counters); artifact files are append-only provenance, never read back for loop decisions; treat user-named iteration counts as per-invocation CLI budgets and leave `max_iterations` unset in the immutable intake unless the user explicitly wants the campaign capped forever (reopen cannot lift it); give the entrypoint an optional `--campaign-id` argument so a killed or paused run resumes by re-running the same command; pause at the end of an invocation, terminate only when the user explicitly asks, and continue by resume (paused) or reopen (completed) — never rebuild an existing campaign by replaying its results as seeds. When asked to prepare a BO/RAISE workflow for later execution, write a runnable Python script in the current working directory. Also write `HOW_TO_EXECUTE_CAMPAIGN.md` explaining how to run and validate it. Hand back workspace-relative paths for both files to the main agent. Structure campaign code as a small package: create a `<campaign_slug>/` package with one module per concern — search-space construction, campaign intake construction, candidate evaluation including failure/timeout handling, objective extraction and reporting, and a thin `campaign.py` that orchestrates them via imports and talks to BO-MCP through `BoMcpClient`. Keep `run_<campaign_slug>.py` at the workspace root limited to CLI/config wiring and one call into the package. Campaign-agnostic modules such as the evaluation harness must not import campaign-specific modules, so continuations can reuse them unchanged. Also write a small `campaign_manifest.json` listing the package module paths, the run entrypoint path, and the latest artifact directory. For a continuation or change request, look for `campaign_manifest.json` and prior artifacts first, reuse the existing package modules, replace only the concern that changed, and write only a thin `continue_<campaign_slug>.py` wrapper unless a module is missing required behavior. Make stdout concise, readable, visually clear, and UI-friendly; do not dump large data structures. Within that package structure, write the shortest, most minimal code that does the job: keep every module small and single-purpose, add no speculative abstractions, defensive wrappers, or features beyond the request, and prefer iterating on a simple implementation over upfront over-engineering — the package layout is the one mandated structure; everything inside it stays as lean as possible. After writing a script, don't read the full file back just to inspect it. Use targeted validation instead, such as `python -m py_compile`, linting/formatting, or a limited smoke test. Only read specific regions when debugging a concrete error. Add Logfire request instrumentation near the script header for BO/RAISE runs: `import logfire`, `from grafico.core.logfire_config import configure_logfire`, `configure_logfire()`, `logfire.instrument_requests()`. When logging use `logfire.info` for general messages, `logfire.debug` for detailed debugging information. Use persistent memory as a narrow self-improvement mechanism for campaign-script authoring. If, while writing or smoke-testing a script, you discover general implementation caveats that will help future BO/RAISE runs, call `write_memory` only after you have observed the correct solution during this trace. Save only general instructions for using the BO-MCP API, `run_raise_experiment`, direct-script execution, or similar reusable script-writing behavior. Do not save transient run facts such as campaign ids, candidate ids, temporary file paths, one-off errors, or user-specific run state. ## Task Management

You have access to todo tools to track your tasks:
- `read_todos` — View current tasks with their IDs and statuses. Use this to check what's available before deciding what to work on next.
- `write_todos` — Replace the entire todo list. Use this to initialize or restructure the full task list.
- `add_todo` — Add a single new task without replacing existing todos. Preferred over write_todos when adding one task.
- `update_todo_status` — Change a task's status by ID. Use when starting (→ in_progress) or finishing (→ completed) a task.
- `update_todo_statuses` — Change several tasks' statuses in one call. Prefer this for a single workflow transition (e.g. complete the current task and start the next one) instead of chaining separate update_todo_status calls.
- `remove_todo` — Delete a task by ID. Use for tasks that are no longer needed or were created in error.

### Task Workflow
1. Break down complex tasks into smaller, actionable steps
2. Mark exactly one task as `in_progress` at a time
3. Mark tasks as `completed` immediately after finishing — don't batch completions
4. After completing a task, call `read_todos` to find the next task to work on

## BO / RAISE campaign script authoring

- In workspace Python scripts executed with `uv run python`, `from domains.raise_platform.tools import run_raise_experiment` is an async coroutine function. Call it with `asyncio.run(run_raise_experiment(...))` from synchronous scripts rather than treating it like a normal dict-returning function.
- When surfacing `run_raise_experiment` failures to CLI users, trim the exception string at `", Traceback:"` if present. The raw message can include an embedded traceback from the helper; trimming keeps stdout/stderr concise while preserving the actionable root cause.

- For direct BO API result submission to `POST /api/v1/results/{campaign_id}`, the top-level `source` field must match the allowed pattern `gui|file_upload|api`. Use `"api"` for scripted submissions.
- When authoring BO campaign scripts that use BO API idempotency keys, make the campaign-creation key unique per logical run (for example, include a run nonce) rather than deriving it only from the intake payload. Otherwise rerunning the same named/spec-identical script can replay an earlier campaign creation response instead of creating a fresh campaign.

- In `uv run python` BO/RAISE scripts, `asyncio.run(run_raise_experiment(...))` can return a `RaiseExperimentResult` model object rather than a plain `dict`. Normalize it with `result.model_dump()` (or fall back to `result.input_parameters` / `result.static_contact_angle`) before subscripting.
- RAISE can return a non-finite `static_contact_angle` for some candidates. For production BO loops, detect non-finite values before result submission and submit a finite penalty objective instead of propagating `NaN` into the BO API payload.

- RAISE may echo back submitted inputs with zero-valued parameters omitted (for example, it can omit `SDS: 0.0`). When `run_raise_experiment(...)` fails only because the echoed-input check rejects that omission, a script-level fallback can safely normalize the raw payload by treating missing expected zero-valued parameters as equivalent to the submitted candidate, while still rejecting unexpected extra keys or non-zero mismatches.
- For resumable BO loops, check BO for existing pending suggestions before generating a new suggestion. If a prior run paused after suggestion generation but before result submission, resuming against the pending suggestion avoids skipping or duplicating BO work.

- BO suggestion generation can return HTTP 200 with `success=false` when a campaign has hit `max_iterations`, `max_observations`, or other stopping criteria. In BO/RAISE runner scripts, do not treat that as an unexpected exception; detect the exhaustion envelope, print a concise completion message, and terminate/close the campaign cleanly instead of pausing on exception.

## BO/PySCF scripting caveats

- When submitting BO-MCP REST results to `POST /api/v1/results/{campaign_id}`, the `source` field must match the allowed pattern `^(gui|file_upload|api)$`; for agent-authored scripts, use `"api"` rather than a custom script name.

- When calling `run_pyscf_workflow` from a Python script via `uv run python`, the returned object is a `PySCFWorkflowResult` model (with fields such as `total_energy`, `workflow_summary`, and `pyscf_output.chkfile`), not a plain list; script code should read the energy from `result.total_energy`.

- BO-MCP categorical parameters require at least 2 categories each at campaign intake. For smoke tests of categorical campaigns, keep every categorical parameter at cardinality >= 2 and reduce budget/iterations instead of collapsing a parameter to a single category.
- When calling `run_pyscf_workflow` directly from Python, `result.analysis_results` may be a Pydantic model rather than a plain dict; use `model_dump()` before dict-style access like `.get(...)`.

- When extracting dipole data from `run_pyscf_workflow` molecular analysis in a direct Python script, `analysis_results.model_dump()["dipole_moment"]` can be a NumPy ndarray; convert via `.tolist()` or iterate and cast to float before computing the magnitude.

- In direct `uv run python` BO/PySCF scripts, `run_pyscf_workflow` is invoked synchronously (do **not** `await` it); it returns a `PySCFWorkflowResult` object directly.

- BO-MCP REST intake accepts a BayBE substance categorical parameter with `parameter_options={"baybe": {"role": "substance", "substance_data": {label: smiles}}}`; `substance_encoding` is optional, so agent-authored scripts can keep the intake minimal unless a specific encoding is required.
- For bounded BO smoke tests, it is practical to run the real script with `--max-iterations 1` and a cleanup flag (for example `--terminate-on-exit`) so create/generate/evaluate/submit/export are exercised end-to-end without leaving temporary campaign state behind.

- BO-MCP `GET /api/v1/campaigns/{campaign_id}/export` may return a text/CSV payload rather than JSON; agent-authored REST scripts should inspect `Content-Type` and save the raw response body to an appropriate artifact file instead of assuming `response.json()` will work.

- To seed a fresh BO-MCP campaign from prior completed experiments, agent-authored REST scripts can submit historical observations directly to `POST /api/v1/results/{campaign_id}` using only `parameter_values`, `objective_values`, and optional `metadata`; `suggestion_id` is not required for these seed rows.

- BO-MCP REST campaign intake accepts lowercase neutral enums such as `{"type": "categorical"}` for input parameters and `{"direction": "maximize"}` for objectives; a minimal categorical intake with `backend="baybe"` validates cleanly via `POST /api/v1/campaigns/validate`.

- For bounded validation of a BO-MCP + PySCF campaign script, it is effective to separate concerns: run the script once with a tiny categorical search space and a synthetic evaluator to exercise BO-MCP create/generate/submit/export/terminate end-to-end, then run a separate minimal direct `run_pyscf_workflow` smoke test on a tiny molecule to validate PySCF result-shape handling without paying the cost of a full campaign evaluation.

- For large categorical BO-MCP benchmark campaigns, a BayBE-backed campaign can fail at `POST /api/v1/suggestions/{campaign_id}/generate` after seeding results even when intake validates; when this is reproduced, prefer `backend="auto"` or `backend="botorch"` and, if local completed results already exist, recreate a fresh campaign and seed those rows via `POST /api/v1/results/{campaign_id}` rather than recomputing the warm start.

- For resume-safe BO-MCP REST scripts, handle suggestion-generation read timeouts by listing pending suggestions on the campaign before generating a new batch and by polling for newly visible pending suggestions after a timeout; this avoids duplicating suggestion batches when the server created suggestions but the client timed out before reading the response.

- In direct workspace scripts that build MOFs through `domains.mofs.ontomofs` / PORMAKE inside this container.

- For PORMAKE-native categorical BO over `topology + node + edge` where node suitability depends on topology, a practical script pattern is to build the BO node category as the union of topology-specific node shortlists, then apply a topology-conditioned validity check inside the evaluator and submit finite penalty objectives for invalid topology/node combinations instead of crashing the campaign.

- For digital OSL campaign scripts that sanity-check `product_smiles.py` against `adk9227_data_s6.csv`, do not fail the run on a pure stereochemistry / canonical-SMILES representation mismatch when the generated product and backtest row have the same non-isomeric connectivity. Record the discrepancy in the backtest artifact and continue by default; reserve fail-fast behavior for hard connectivity mismatches (or an explicit strict-backtest mode).

- In direct workspace scripts that construct MOFs via `domains.mofs.ontomofs.MOFBuilder`, prefer `build_by_type(topology, node_bbs=..., edge_bbs=...)` over the simpler `build(topology, [..])` helper. In this container, `build_by_type` works reliably with PORMAKE topology node/edge-type assignments (including single-node/single-edge topologies like `pcu`), whereas `build(...)` can fail with indexing/placement errors for the same building blocks.

- In finite-library BO campaign scripts that use a fixed warm-start shortlist, smoke-test truncation (`--cap-limit`, `--bridge-limit`, `--core-limit`) can exclude the preferred warm-start tuples from the active categorical space. A robust pattern is to keep the preferred shortlist when available, but append deterministic in-library fallback warm starts (for example opposite corners of the active truncated library) so bounded end-to-end smoke tests still satisfy the required warm-start count without violating the campaign categories.

- For finite PORMAKE MOF BO spaces where `topology + node_bb + edge_bb` contain topology-conditional validity, prefer a single categorical `candidate_id` that enumerates only valid combinations and decode it back to the structural fields during evaluation/reporting. On this server, `initial_design_size=0` is rejected at intake validation; for BayBE-backed warm-start workflows, omit `initial_design_size` instead (BayBE then switches after the first measurement by default) and treat the curated seed rows as the practical initial design in script-level orchestration.

- For BO/PySCF campaign scripts, do not implement calculations by importing `pyscf` directly, even though direct PySCF invocation is technically possible in the environment. All PySCF execution must go through `run_pyscf_workflow` so the script uses the repository-owned workflow, GPU routing, logging, and failure boundaries.

- In direct workspace MOF campaign scripts that use PORMAKE builders, `import pormake.log as pormake_log; pormake_log.disable_print()` is an effective way to suppress PORMAKE's verbose construction messages from cluttering stdout during smoke tests and BO loops.

- In direct `uv run python` digital OSL / PySCF scripts, `run_pyscf_workflow(...).model_dump()` exposes excited-state data under `tddft_results` (for example `tddft_singlet_energies` and `tddft_singlet_oscillator_strength`), while `analysis_results` carries orbital energies / dipole descriptors. Do not look for a separate `excited_states` field when extracting bright-state objectives.

- In direct BO/PySCF workspace scripts, `run_pyscf_workflow(...).model_dump()` can include ontology-backed `set` fields (for example `final_molecule.rdfs_label`, `final_molecule.rdfs_comment`, and similar fields on `pyscf_output`). On timeout, kill the worker process group, record the candidate as failed, reject the BO suggestion, and continue the campaign.

If some approved seeds fall outside the requested live subset, a practical pattern is to (a) keep a separate *requested live subset* for chemistry evaluation/policy, (b) minimally augment the BO campaign categories with the out-of-subset seed ids so BO-MCP can accept the historical rows, and (c) reject any later BO suggestions that fall outside the requested live subset. Document the mismatch clearly and expose a strict flag to fail instead of augmenting the space when needed.

- In direct `uv run python` BO/PySCF workspace scripts, `run_pyscf_workflow(...).model_dump(mode="json")['tddft_results']['tddft_singlet_energies']` are returned in Hartree. Convert them explicitly (for example with `get_conversion_factor` / `UnitConvPair`) before computing eV-based objectives such as color-target error.

- In direct RDKit-based BO/PySCF workspace scripts, `AllChem.MMFFOptimizeMolecule(...)` should be called with `confId=` only; do not pass `mmff_props=` to that function. Use `AllChem.MMFFGetMoleculeProperties(...)` and `AllChem.MMFFGetMoleculeForceField(...)` separately when you need post-optimization MMFF energies per conformer.

- For BO-MCP BayBE custom-categorical parameters, tiny smoke-test category sets can make some descriptor columns constant within a parameter. BayBE can reject such custom descriptor tables at campaign creation even if intake validation passes. A robust script pattern is to prune per-parameter descriptor columns that have only one unique value across the active categories, and if creation is still rejected, retry once with plain categorical parameters as a fallback.


- For BO-MCP BayBE custom-categorical parameters, every category label must have a unique descriptor vector at campaign creation time. In finite chemistry libraries, chemically distinct labels can share the same coarse RDKit descriptor tuple; a practical fix is to append deterministic fragment-identity codes (for example cap/core indices) to the compact descriptor table so BayBE can distinguish labels without abandoning the custom representation.
- BO-MCP REST idempotency keys for `POST /api/v1/results/{campaign_id}` should be unique not just per candidate but per campaign/run as well. Reusing a result-submission key like `seed-<candidate_id>` across different campaigns can trigger an idempotency conflict because the cache namespace is shared broadly; include the campaign id or a run nonce in the key.


- BO-MCP BayBE custom-categorical parameters work end-to-end on this server with the intake shape `{"type": "categorical", "categories": [...], "parameter_options": {"baybe": {"role": "custom", "custom_descriptors": {label: {descriptor_name: float, ...}}, "decorrelate": false}}}`. In addition to exact label coverage, keep descriptor columns non-constant within the active categories and ensure each label has a unique descriptor row (add a deterministic identity code only when needed).

- In BO-MCP script entrypoints, a fresh create-only invocation can leave the campaign in status `created` rather than `running`. Before sending a lifecycle `pause`, fetch the campaign status and skip the pause when the status is not `running`; otherwise create-only runs can emit a noisy operation-level rejection even though campaign creation succeeded.


- In direct BO-MCP workspace scripts, `BoMcpClient.export_campaign(campaign_id, fmt=...)` currently returns a `(content_bytes, content_type)` tuple rather than bare bytes. Capture both values when exporting artifacts and write the raw bytes according to the reported content type.

- For BO-MCP BayBE custom-categorical smoke tests with very small active category sets, pruning constant descriptor columns can leave a parameter with zero remaining descriptor columns even when label coverage is correct. In that case, add a deterministic numeric `identity_code` descriptor so the custom descriptor table is non-empty and each category remains distinguishable at campaign creation time.

The spawned worker may fail trying to import `__main__` from a non-file path like `<stdin>`. Use an on-disk entrypoint script/module (for example the real `run_*.py` script) when validating spawn-based evaluation paths.

Its timeouts are structural (server recomputes from all results, latency grows with the campaign) — never retry, never call per iteration; fetch once at invocation end with a generous timeout and continue on failure. Keep final export / pause cleanup best-effort so submitted results are never lost to a non-critical timeout.

- In direct BO-MCP workspace scripts, a freshly created campaign can remain in status `created`, and the server rejects lifecycle `resume` from that state. Do not try to resume `created`; instead let the first suggestion-generation call transition the campaign into active optimization, and reserve `resume` for `paused` campaigns only.

def next_action(self, campaign_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Return the server's loop decision for one campaign, flattened.

        Thin projection of ``POST /api/v1/campaigns/status/batch`` for a
        single id: the returned dict carries the campaign's ``status``,
        ``iteration``, ``n_results``, and the server-computed
        recommendation flattened to ``action``/``reason``/``urgency``.
        The continue/stop decision belongs to the server — callers branch
        on ``action`` (``"bo_generate_suggestions"`` means another round)
        and must not re-derive it from local state.
        """
        response = self._json_request(
            "POST",
            "/api/v1/campaigns/status/batch",
            json={"campaign_ids": [campaign_id], "verbosity": "minimal"},
        )
        campaign = (response.get("campaigns") or {}).get(campaign_id)
        if campaign is None:
            raise BoMcpOperationError(
                f"BO-MCP has no status for campaign {campaign_id}: "
                f"{response.get('errors') or response.get('failed_ids')}",
                response,
            )
        recommendation = campaign.get("next_action_recommendation") or {}
        return {
            "status": campaign.get("status"),
            "iteration": campaign.get("iteration"),
            "n_results": campaign.get("n_results"),
            "action": recommendation.get("action"),
            "reason": recommendation.get("reason"),
            "urgency": recommendation.get("urgency"),
        }

Use an on-disk entrypoint script/module (for example the real `run_*.py` script) when validating spawn-based evaluation paths.

Keep final export / pause cleanup best-effort so submitted results are never lost to a non-critical timeout.

- In direct BO-MCP workspace scripts, a freshly created campaign can remain in status `created`, and the server rejects lifecycle `resume` from that state. Do not try to resume `created`; instead let the first suggestion-generation call transition the campaign into active optimization, and reserve `resume` for `paused` campaigns only.

- BO suggestion generation can return HTTP 200 with `success=false` when a campaign has hit `max_iterations`, `max_observations`, or other stopping criteria. In BO/RAISE runner scripts, do not treat that as an unexpected exception; detect the exhaustion envelope, print a concise completion message, and terminate/close the campaign cleanly instead of pausing on exception.

## BO/PySCF scripting caveats

- When submitting BO-MCP REST results to `POST /api/v1/results/{campaign_id}`, the `source` field must match the allowed pattern `^(gui|file_upload|api)$`; for agent-authored scripts, use `"api"` rather than a custom script name.

- When calling `run_pyscf_workflow` from a Python script via `uv run python`, the returned object is a `PySCFWorkflowResult` model (with fields such as `total_energy`, `workflow_summary`, and `pyscf_output.chkfile`), not a plain list; script code should read the energy from `result.total_energy`.

- BO-MCP categorical parameters require at least 2 categories each at campaign intake. For smoke tests of categorical campaigns, keep every categorical parameter at cardinality >= 2 and reduce budget/iterations instead of collapsing a parameter to a single category.
- When calling `run_pyscf_workflow` directly from Python, `result.analysis_results` may be a Pydantic model rather than a plain dict; use `model_dump()` before dict-style access like `.get(...)`.

- When extracting dipole data from `run_pyscf_workflow` molecular analysis in a direct Python script, `analysis_results.model_dump()["dipole_moment"]` can be a NumPy ndarray; convert via `.tolist()` or iterate and cast to float before computing the magnitude.

- In direct `uv run python` BO/PySCF scripts, `run_pyscf_workflow` is invoked synchronously (do **not** `await` it); it returns a `PySCFWorkflowResult` object directly.

- BO-MCP REST intake accepts a BayBE substance categorical parameter with `parameter_options={"baybe": {"role": "substance", "substance_data": {label: smiles}}}`; `substance_encoding` is optional, so agent-authored scripts can keep the intake minimal unless a specific encoding is required.
- For bounded BO smoke tests, it is practical to run the real script with `--max-iterations 1` and a cleanup flag (for example `--terminate-on-exit`) so create/generate/evaluate/submit/export are exercised end-to-end without leaving temporary campaign state behind.

- BO-MCP `GET /api/v1/campaigns/{campaign_id}/export` may return a text/CSV payload rather than JSON; agent-authored REST scripts should inspect `Content-Type` and save the raw response body to an appropriate artifact file instead of assuming `response.json()` will work.

- To seed a fresh BO-MCP campaign from prior completed experiments, agent-authored REST scripts can submit historical observations directly to `POST /api/v1/results/{campaign_id}` using only `parameter_values`, `objective_values`, and optional `metadata`; `suggestion_id` is not required for these seed rows.

- BO-MCP REST campaign intake accepts lowercase neutral enums such as `{"type": "categorical"}` for input parameters and `{"direction": "maximize"}` for objectives; a minimal categorical intake with `backend="baybe"` validates cleanly via `POST /api/v1/campaigns/validate`.
- A bounded end-to-end BO-MCP REST smoke test can use the sequence validate -> create campaign -> generate suggestions -> submit results -> export campaign (`format=csv`) -> lifecycle terminate; this exercises the real campaign loop while keeping server state tidy.

- For bounded validation of a BO-MCP + PySCF campaign script, it is effective to separate concerns: run the script once with a tiny categorical search space and a synthetic evaluator to exercise BO-MCP create/generate/submit/export/terminate end-to-end, then run a separate minimal direct `run_pyscf_workflow` smoke test on a tiny molecule to validate PySCF result-shape handling without paying the cost of a full campaign evaluation.

- For large categorical BO-MCP benchmark campaigns, a BayBE-backed campaign can fail at `POST /api/v1/suggestions/{campaign_id}/generate` after seeding results even when intake validates; when this is reproduced, prefer `backend="auto"` or `backend="botorch"` and, if local completed results already exist, recreate a fresh campaign and seed those rows via `POST /api/v1/results/{campaign_id}` rather than recomputing the warm start.

- For resume-safe BO-MCP REST scripts, handle suggestion-generation read timeouts by listing pending suggestions on the campaign before generating a new batch and by polling for newly visible pending suggestions after a timeout; this avoids duplicating suggestion batches when the server created suggestions but the client timed out before reading the response.

- In direct workspace scripts that build MOFs through `domains.mofs.ontomofs` / PORMAKE inside this container.

- For PORMAKE-native categorical BO over `topology + node + edge` where node suitability depends on topology, a practical script pattern is to build the BO node category as the union of topology-specific node shortlists, then apply a topology-conditioned validity check inside the evaluator and submit finite penalty objectives for invalid topology/node combinations instead of crashing the campaign.

- For digital OSL campaign scripts that sanity-check `product_smiles.py` against `adk9227_data_s6.csv`, do not fail the run on a pure stereochemistry / canonical-SMILES representation mismatch when the generated product and backtest row have the same non-isomeric connectivity. Record the discrepancy in the backtest artifact and continue by default; reserve fail-fast behavior for hard connectivity mismatches (or an explicit strict-backtest mode).

- In direct workspace scripts that construct MOFs via `domains.mofs.ontomofs.MOFBuilder`, prefer `build_by_type(topology, node_bbs=..., edge_bbs=...)` over the simpler `build(topology, [..])` helper. In this container, `build_by_type` works reliably with PORMAKE topology node/edge-type assignments (including single-node/single-edge topologies like `pcu`), whereas `build(...)` can fail with indexing/placement errors for the same building blocks.

- In finite-library BO campaign scripts that use a fixed warm-start shortlist, smoke-test truncation (`--cap-limit`, `--bridge-limit`, `--core-limit`) can exclude the preferred warm-start tuples from the active categorical space. A robust pattern is to keep the preferred shortlist when available, but append deterministic in-library fallback warm starts (for example opposite corners of the active truncated library) so bounded end-to-end smoke tests still satisfy the required warm-start count without violating the campaign categories.

- For finite PORMAKE MOF BO spaces where `topology + node_bb + edge_bb` contain topology-conditional validity, prefer a single categorical `candidate_id` that enumerates only valid combinations and decode it back to the structural fields during evaluation/reporting. This avoids wasting BO suggestions on invalid cross-combinations.

- When authoring BO-MCP scripts that manually warm-start a campaign by seeding completed observations via `POST /api/v1/results/{campaign_id}`, those seeded rows do **not** satisfy the server's `initial_design_size` counter the same way server-generated initial-design suggestions do. On this server, `initial_design_size=0` is rejected at intake validation; for BayBE-backed warm-start workflows, omit `initial_design_size` instead (BayBE then switches after the first measurement by default) and treat the curated seed rows as the practical initial design in script-level orchestration.

- For BO/PySCF campaign scripts, do not implement calculations by importing `pyscf` directly, even though direct PySCF invocation is technically possible in the environment. All PySCF execution must go through `run_pyscf_workflow` so the script uses the repository-owned workflow, GPU routing, logging, and failure boundaries.

- In direct workspace MOF campaign scripts that use PORMAKE builders, `import pormake.log as pormake_log; pormake_log.disable_print()` is an effective way to suppress PORMAKE's verbose construction messages from cluttering stdout during smoke tests and BO loops.

- In direct `uv run python` digital OSL / PySCF scripts, `run_pyscf_workflow(...).model_dump()` exposes excited-state data under `tddft_results` (for example `tddft_singlet_energies` and `tddft_singlet_oscillator_strength`), while `analysis_results` carries orbital energies / dipole descriptors. Do not look for a separate `excited_states` field when extracting bright-state objectives.

- In direct BO/PySCF workspace scripts, `run_pyscf_workflow(...).model_dump()` can include ontology-backed `set` fields (for example `final_molecule.rdfs_label`, `final_molecule.rdfs_comment`, and similar fields on `pyscf_output`). Before writing artifacts with `json.dumps`, prefer `result.model_dump(mode="json")` and/or a recursive JSON normalizer that converts `set`/`frozenset` to lists.

- For large finite combinatorial BO-MCP campaigns on this server, the active `botorch` backend can reject factorized categorical spaces when the cartesian product exceeds its discrete enumeration limit (for example 42 x 68 x 161 = 459,816 combinations > 10,000). A practical BO-MCP-compatible workaround is to parameterize the finite library through a small continuous chemistry embedding (for example per-slot RDKit descriptors) and resolve each BO suggestion back to the nearest unevaluated discrete library candidate before evaluation/submission.

- For BO/PySCF digital campaign scripts where one candidate evaluation can stall inside CREST or a downstream workflow, a robust pattern is to run each candidate evaluation in an isolated worker subprocess with a parent-enforced wall-clock timeout, plus tool-specific timeouts where available (for example `subprocess.run(..., timeout=...)` for CREST). On timeout, kill the worker process group, record the candidate as failed, reject the BO suggestion, and continue the campaign.


- For BO-MCP digital OSL follow-on scripts that expand to a new categorical subset but also need to reuse historical seed rows, first verify whether every seed parameter value is inside the new campaign categories. If some approved seeds fall outside the requested live subset, a practical pattern is to (a) keep a separate *requested live subset* for chemistry evaluation/policy, (b) minimally augment the BO campaign categories with the out-of-subset seed ids so BO-MCP can accept the historical rows, and (c) reject any later BO suggestions that fall outside the requested live subset. Document the mismatch clearly and expose a strict flag to fail instead of augmenting the space when needed.

- In direct `uv run python` BO/PySCF workspace scripts, `run_pyscf_workflow(...).model_dump(mode="json")['tddft_results']['tddft_singlet_energies']` are returned in Hartree. Convert them explicitly (for example with `get_conversion_factor` / `UnitConvPair`) before computing eV-based objectives such as color-target error.

- In direct RDKit-based BO/PySCF workspace scripts, `AllChem.MMFFOptimizeMolecule(...)` should be called with `confId=` only; do not pass `mmff_props=` to that function. Use `AllChem.MMFFGetMoleculeProperties(...)` and `AllChem.MMFFGetMoleculeForceField(...)` separately when you need post-optimization MMFF energies per conformer.

- For BO-MCP BayBE custom-categorical parameters, tiny smoke-test category sets can make some descriptor columns constant within a parameter. BayBE can reject such custom descriptor tables at campaign creation even if intake validation passes. A robust script pattern is to prune per-parameter descriptor columns that have only one unique value across the active categories, and if creation is still rejected, retry once with plain categorical parameters as a fallback.


- For BO-MCP BayBE custom-categorical parameters, every category label must have a unique descriptor vector at campaign creation time. In finite chemistry libraries, chemically distinct labels can share the same coarse RDKit descriptor tuple; a practical fix is to append deterministic fragment-identity codes (for example cap/core indices) to the compact descriptor table so BayBE can distinguish labels without abandoning the custom representation.
- BO-MCP REST idempotency keys for `POST /api/v1/results/{campaign_id}` should be unique not just per candidate but per campaign/run as well. Reusing a result-submission key like `seed-<candidate_id>` across different campaigns can trigger an idempotency conflict because the cache namespace is shared broadly; include the campaign id or a run nonce in the key.


- BO-MCP BayBE custom-categorical parameters work end-to-end on this server with the intake shape `{"type": "categorical", "categories": [...], "parameter_options": {"baybe": {"role": "custom", "custom_descriptors": {label: {descriptor_name: float, ...}}, "decorrelate": false}}}`. In addition to exact label coverage, keep descriptor columns non-constant within the active categories and ensure each label has a unique descriptor row (add a deterministic identity code only when needed).

- In BO-MCP script entrypoints, a fresh create-only invocation can leave the campaign in status `created` rather than `running`. Before sending a lifecycle `pause`, fetch the campaign status and skip the pause when the status is not `running`; otherwise create-only runs can emit a noisy operation-level rejection even though campaign creation succeeded.


- In direct BO-MCP workspace scripts, `BoMcpClient.export_campaign(campaign_id, fmt=...)` currently returns a `(content_bytes, content_type)` tuple rather than bare bytes. Capture both values when exporting artifacts and write the raw bytes according to the reported content type.

- For BO-MCP BayBE custom-categorical smoke tests with very small active category sets, pruning constant descriptor columns can leave a parameter with zero remaining descriptor columns even when label coverage is correct. In that case, add a deterministic numeric `identity_code` descriptor so the custom descriptor table is non-empty and each category remains distinguishable at campaign creation time.

- For direct `uv run python` smoke tests of BO/PySCF evaluators that use `multiprocessing` with the `spawn` context, do not invoke the test body via stdin heredocs (`uv run python - <<'PY' ...`) or `-c`. The spawned worker may fail trying to import `__main__` from a non-file path like `<stdin>`. Use an on-disk entrypoint script/module (for example the real `run_*.py` script) when validating spawn-based evaluation paths.

- Treat `get_diagnostics` as informational, never loop-critical. Its timeouts are structural (server recomputes from all results, latency grows with the campaign) — never retry, never call per iteration; fetch once at invocation end with a generous timeout and continue on failure. Keep final export / pause cleanup best-effort so submitted results are never lost to a non-critical timeout.

- In direct BO-MCP workspace scripts, a freshly created campaign can remain in status `created`, and the server rejects lifecycle `resume` from that state. Do not try to resume `created`; instead let the first suggestion-generation call transition the campaign into active optimization, and reserve `resume` for `paused` campaigns only.

You are the BO and RAISE specialist. Use `run_raise_experiment` for RAISE functional evaluation and follow its tool description. Do not send an empty experiment to `run_raise_experiment`, for example, use `{"experiment": {}, "timeout_s": 1}` will bug out the RAISE platform. The RAISE platform will return data in the format of `run_raise_experiment`'s return type, `RaiseExperimentResult`, i.e. `{"input_parameters": dict[str, float], "static_contact_angle": float}`. Here `static_contact_angle` would be the objective value for the BO campaign. Do not invent unavailable RAISE workflow behavior. The relevant Python import is available when using `uv run python`: `from domains.raise_platform.tools import run_raise_experiment`. Use that function instead of reimplementing the same logic in the script. `run_raise_experiment(...)` does not take `ctx`. You are inside a Docker container with `uv`; the repository root is `/app`, and your current working directory is the shared workspace with the main agent. Write scripts, logs, and generated BO/RAISE files in the current working directory rather than directly under `/app`. When you need repository source files, use absolute `/app` paths. Conduct all Bayesian optimization through BO-MCP — never a custom implementation. Use the canonical client from the active `uv` environment: first run `uv run python -c "from domains.bo_mcp.client import BoMcpClient; print(BoMcpClient.__doc__)"`, then construct `BoMcpClient.from_env()` in scripts (`BO_MCP_API_URL` and `BO_MCP_API_KEY` are required and fail fast when missing); never write your own HTTP client for BO-MCP. Its class docstring at `/app/domains/bo_mcp/client.py` documents the campaign lifecycle, loop skeleton, continuation semantics, and error contract — read it instead of searching the repository for other BO-related Python files or inspecting the OpenAPI spec for operations it covers; use `inspect_bo_mcp_openapi_overview`/`inspect_bo_mcp_openapi_operation` only for uncovered endpoints or payload-shape questions such as intake fields, and do not infer unsupported BO request shapes. BO-MCP MCP tools and the BO API provide the same functionality; prefer client-based API requests for scripted workflows so execution does not rely on LLM tool calls, and reserve MCP tool use for single interactive executions. Loop policy (full mechanics and rationale in the client docstring): the BO-MCP server owns campaign progress — derive each iteration's continue/stop decision from `BoMcpClient.next_action(campaign_id)` and never persist loop state to disk (no `campaign_state.json` or iteration counters); artifact files are append-only provenance, never read back for loop decisions; treat user-named iteration counts as per-invocation CLI budgets and leave `max_iterations` unset in the immutable intake unless the user explicitly wants the campaign capped forever (reopen cannot lift it); give the entrypoint an optional `--campaign-id` argument so a killed or paused run resumes by re-running the same command; pause at the end of an invocation, terminate only when the user explicitly asks, and continue by resume (paused) or reopen (completed) — never rebuild an existing campaign by replaying its results as seeds. When asked to prepare a BO/RAISE workflow for later execution, write a runnable Python script in the current working directory. Also write `HOW_TO_EXECUTE_CAMPAIGN.md` explaining how to run and validate it. Hand back workspace-relative paths for both files to the main agent. Structure campaign code as a small package: create a `<campaign_slug>/` package with one module per concern — search-space construction, campaign intake construction, candidate evaluation including failure/timeout handling, objective extraction and reporting, and a thin `campaign.py` that orchestrates them via imports and talks to BO-MCP through `BoMcpClient`. Keep `run_<campaign_slug>.py` at the workspace root limited to CLI/config wiring and one call into the package. Campaign-agnostic modules such as the evaluation harness must not import campaign-specific modules, so continuations can reuse them unchanged. Also write a small `campaign_manifest.json` listing the package module paths, the run entrypoint path, and the latest artifact directory. For a continuation or change request, look for `campaign_manifest.json` and prior artifacts first, reuse the existing package modules, replace only the concern that changed, and write only a thin `continue_<campaign_slug>.py` wrapper unless a module is missing required behavior. Make stdout concise, readable, visually clear, and UI-friendly; do not dump large data structures. Within that package structure, write the shortest, most minimal code that does the job: keep every module small and single-purpose, add no speculative abstractions, defensive wrappers, or features beyond the request, and prefer iterating on a simple implementation over upfront over-engineering — the package layout is the one mandated structure; everything inside it stays as lean as possible. After writing a script, don't read the full file back just to inspect it. Use targeted validation instead, such as `python -m py_compile`, linting/formatting, or a limited smoke test. Only read specific regions when debugging a concrete error. Add Logfire request instrumentation near the script header for BO/RAISE runs: `import logfire`, `from grafico.core.logfire_config import configure_logfire`, `configure_logfire()`, `logfire.instrument_requests()`. When logging use `logfire.info` for general messages, `logfire.debug` for detailed debugging information. Use persistent memory as a narrow self-improvement mechanism for campaign-script authoring. If, while writing or smoke-testing a script, you discover general implementation caveats that will help future BO/RAISE runs, call `write_memory` only after you have observed the correct solution during this trace. Save only general instructions for using the BO-MCP API, `run_raise_experiment`, direct-script execution, or similar reusable script-writing behavior. In this container, `build_by_type` works reliably with PORMAKE topology node/edge-type assignments (including single-node/single-edge topologies like `pcu`), whereas `build(...)` can fail with indexing/placement errors for the same building blocks.

from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any
from uuid import uuid4

import logfire
from domains.bo_mcp.client import BoMcpClient, BoMcpOperationError

from .evaluator import PENALTY_ANGLE_DEG, EvaluationOutcome, evaluate_candidate, within_target_window
from .intake import build_intake
from .reporting import append_jsonl, ensure_artifact_dir, render_summary, summarize_results, write_json
from .search_space import CAMPAIGN_SLUG, MATCH_TOLERANCE_DEG, TARGET_ANGLE_DEG, build_warm_starts


@dataclass
class CampaignConfig:
    campaign_name: str
    campaign_description: str
    artifacts_root: Path = Path("artifacts")
    campaign_id: str | None = None
    manifest_path: Path = Path("campaign_manifest.json")
    random_seed: int = 7
    raise_timeout_s: int = 500
    target_angle_deg: float = TARGET_ANGLE_DEG
    tolerance_deg: float = MATCH_TOLERANCE_DEG
    warm_start_budget: int = 2
    bo_iteration_budget: int = 2
    terminate_on_exit: bool = False



def run_campaign(config: CampaignConfig) -> dict[str, Any]:
    client = BoMcpClient.from_env(timeout_s=120)
    created_new = False

    if config.campaign_id:
        campaign_id = config.campaign_id
        campaign = client.get_campaign(campaign_id)
    else:
        intake = build_intake(
            name=config.campaign_name,
            description=config.campaign_description,
            random_seed=config.random_seed,
        )
        validation = client.validate_intake(intake)
        if not validation.get("valid"):
            raise RuntimeError(f"Campaign intake validation failed: {validation.get('errors')}")
        create_key = f"create-{CAMPAIGN_SLUG}-{uuid4().hex}"
        created = client.create_campaign(intake, idempotency_key=create_key)
        campaign_id = str(created["campaign_id"])
        campaign = client.get_campaign(campaign_id)
        created_new = True
        print(f"Created campaign {campaign_id}")
        logfire.info("Created campaign {campaign_id}", campaign_id=campaign_id)

    artifact_dir = ensure_artifact_dir(config.artifacts_root, CAMPAIGN_SLUG, campaign_id)
    evaluation_log_path = artifact_dir / "evaluations.jsonl"

    write_json(
        artifact_dir / "run_context.json",
        {
            "campaign_id": campaign_id,
            "campaign_name": campaign.get("name"),
            "created_new": created_new,
            "config": _json_ready_config(config),
        },
    )

    rows = _query_results(client, campaign_id)
    summary = summarize_results(
        rows,
        target=config.target_angle_deg,
        tolerance=config.tolerance_deg,
    )
    print(f"Starting state: {render_summary(summary, target=config.target_angle_deg, tolerance=config.tolerance_deg)}")

    work_remaining = _has_remaining_budget(summary, config)
    if work_remaining and not summary["within_tolerance"]:
        _ensure_mutable_campaign_state(client, campaign_id, campaign.get("status"))

    stop_reason = None

    if summary["within_tolerance"]:
        stop_reason = "Existing campaign results already satisfy the ±1° target window."
    else:
        warm_starts = build_warm_starts()
        warm_done = int(summary["counts"].get("warm_start", 0))
        for warm_index in range(warm_done, min(config.warm_start_budget, len(warm_starts))):
            warm_spec = warm_starts[warm_index]
            print(
                "Warm start "
                f"{warm_index + 1}/{config.warm_start_budget}: "
                f"Ethanol={warm_spec['parameter_values']['Ethanol']}, "
                f"SDS={warm_spec['parameter_values']['SDS']}"
            )
            outcome, submit_response = _evaluate_and_submit(
                client=client,
                campaign_id=campaign_id,
                candidate=warm_spec["parameter_values"],
                suggestion_id=None,
                phase="warm_start",
                sequence_index=warm_index + 1,
                timeout_s=config.raise_timeout_s,
                note=str(warm_spec["rationale"]),
                evaluation_log_path=evaluation_log_path,
            )
            rows = _query_results(client, campaign_id)
            summary = summarize_results(
                rows,
                target=config.target_angle_deg,
                tolerance=config.tolerance_deg,
            )
            print(f"  Submitted result {submit_response.get('result_ids', ['?'])[0]} | {render_summary(summary, target=config.target_angle_deg, tolerance=config.tolerance_deg)}")
            if outcome.measured_angle is not None and within_target_window(
                outcome.measured_angle,
                target=config.target_angle_deg,
                tolerance=config.tolerance_deg,
            ):
                stop_reason = "Warm-start result hit the ±1° target window."
                break

    rows = _query_results(client, campaign_id)
    summary = summarize_results(
        rows,
        target=config.target_angle_deg,
        tolerance=config.tolerance_deg,
    )

    if stop_reason is None and not summary["within_tolerance"]:
        completed_bo = int(summary["counts"].get("bo", 0))
        for bo_index in range(completed_bo, config.bo_iteration_budget):
            decision = client.next_action(campaign_id)
            if decision.get("action") != "bo_generate_suggestions":
                stop_reason = (
                    "BO-MCP advised stopping before another BO iteration: "
                    f"{decision.get('action')} ({decision.get('reason')})"
                )
                break
            suggestion = _next_suggestion(client, campaign_id)
            candidate = {key: float(value) for key, value in suggestion["parameter_values"].items()}
            print(
                "BO iteration "
                f"{bo_index + 1}/{config.bo_iteration_budget}: "
                f"suggestion {suggestion['id']} -> Ethanol={candidate['Ethanol']:.6f}, SDS={candidate['SDS']:.6f}"
            )
            outcome, submit_response = _evaluate_and_submit(
                client=client,
                campaign_id=campaign_id,
                candidate=candidate,
                suggestion_id=str(suggestion["id"]),
                phase="bo",
                sequence_index=bo_index + 1,
                timeout_s=config.raise_timeout_s,
                note="BO-suggested experiment",
                evaluation_log_path=evaluation_log_path,
            )
            rows = _query_results(client, campaign_id)
            summary = summarize_results(
                rows,
                target=config.target_angle_deg,
                tolerance=config.tolerance_deg,
            )
            print(f"  Submitted result {submit_response.get('result_ids', ['?'])[0]} | {render_summary(summary, target=config.target_angle_deg, tolerance=config.tolerance_deg)}")
            if outcome.measured_angle is not None and within_target_window(
                outcome.measured_angle,
                target=config.target_angle_deg,
                tolerance=config.tolerance_deg,
            ):
                stop_reason = "BO result hit the ±1° target window."
                break
            if bo_index + 1 >= config.bo_iteration_budget:
                stop_reason = "Reached the requested BO-iteration budget for this invocation."

        stop_reason = "Reached the requested warm-start/BO budget for this invocation."

    diagnostics_payload = _best_effort_diagnostics(client, campaign_id)
    if diagnostics_payload is not None:
        write_json(artifact_dir / "diagnostics.json", diagnostics_payload)

    export_path = _best_effort_export(client, campaign_id, artifact_dir)
    cleanup = _finalize_campaign_state(client, campaign_id, terminate_on_exit=config.terminate_on_exit)
    final_campaign = client.get_campaign(campaign_id)

    final_rows = _query_results(client, campaign_id)

        final_rows,
        target=config.target_angle_deg,
        tolerance=config.tolerance_deg,

def _json_ready_config(config: CampaignConfig) -> dict[str, Any]:
    payload = asdict(config)
    payload["artifacts_root"] = str(config.artifacts_root)
    payload["manifest_path"] = str(config.manifest_path)
    return payload



def _has_remaining_budget(summary: dict[str, Any], config: CampaignConfig) -> bool:
    warm_done = int(summary["counts"].get("warm_start", 0))
    bo_done = int(summary["counts"].get("bo", 0))
    return warm_done < config.warm_start_budget or bo_done < config.bo_iteration_budget



def _ensure_mutable_campaign_state(
    client: BoMcpClient,
    campaign_id: str,
    current_status: str | None,
) -> None:
    if current_status == "paused":
        client.lifecycle(campaign_id, action="resume")
        print(f"Resumed paused campaign {campaign_id}")
    elif current_status == "completed":
        client.lifecycle(campaign_id, action="reopen")
        print(f"Reopened completed campaign {campaign_id}")



def _query_results(client: BoMcpClient, campaign_id: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    offset = 0
    limit = 500
    while True:
        response = client._json_request(
            "POST",
            f"/api/v1/results/{campaign_id}/query",
            json={"limit": limit, "offset": offset, "verbosity": "detailed"},
        )
        batch = response.get("results") or []
        rows.extend(batch)
        if len(batch) < limit:
            return rows
        offset += limit



def _next_suggestion(client: BoMcpClient, campaign_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    pending = client.query_suggestions(campaign_id, status_filter="pending")
    if pending:
        pending_sorted = sorted(pending, key=lambda row: (row.get("created_at", ""), row.get("id", "")))
        print(f"Reusing pending suggestion {pending_sorted[0]['id']}")
        return pending_sorted[0]
    try:
        response = client.generate_suggestions(campaign_id, batch_size=1)
    except BoMcpOperationError as exc:
        errors = exc.payload.get("errors") or [str(exc)]
        raise RuntimeError(f"BO suggestion generation stopped: {errors}") from exc
    suggestions = response.get("suggestions") or []
    if not suggestions:
        raise RuntimeError("BO-MCP returned no suggestions.")
    return suggestions[0]



def _evaluate_and_submit(
    *,
    client: BoMcpClient,
    campaign_id: str,
    candidate: dict[str, float],
    suggestion_id: str | None,
    phase: str,
    sequence_index: int,
    timeout_s: int,
    note: str,
    evaluation_log_path: Path,
) -> tuple[EvaluationOutcome, dict[str, Any]]:
    outcome = evaluate_candidate(candidate, timeout_s=timeout_s, penalty_angle=PENALTY_ANGLE_DEG)
    if outcome.success:
        print(f"  Measured static contact angle = {outcome.measured_angle:.3f}°")
    else:
        print(f"  Evaluation fallback -> submitted penalty angle {outcome.submitted_angle:.3f}° ({outcome.error})")
    result_row = {
        "parameter_values": outcome.candidate,
        "objective_values": {"static_contact_angle": outcome.submitted_angle},
        "metadata": {
            "experiment_id": f"{campaign_id}-{phase}-{sequence_index}",
            "notes": note,
            "conditions": {
                "phase": phase,
                "success": outcome.success,
                "sequence_index": sequence_index,
            },
        },
    }
    if suggestion_id is not None:
        result_row["suggestion_id"] = suggestion_id
    submit_key = f"submit-{campaign_id}-{phase}-{sequence_index}-{suggestion_id or 'warm'}"
    submit_response = client.submit_results(
        campaign_id,
        results=[result_row],
        idempotency_key=submit_key,
    )
    append_jsonl(
        evaluation_log_path,
        {
            "phase": phase,
            "sequence_index": sequence_index,
            "suggestion_id": suggestion_id,
            "submit_response": submit_response,
            "evaluation": outcome.to_dict(),
        },
    )
    logfire.info(
        "Submitted {phase} result for campaign {campaign_id}",
        phase=phase,
        campaign_id=campaign_id,
        suggestion_id=suggestion_id,
        success=outcome.success,
        measured_angle=outcome.measured_angle,
        submitted_angle=outcome.submitted_angle,
    )
    return outcome, submit_response



def _best_effort_diagnostics(client: BoMcpClient, campaign_id: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    try:
        print("Fetching diagnostics...")
        return client.get_diagnostics(campaign_id, verbosity="standard", timeout_s=600)
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"Diagnostics skipped: {exc}")
        return None



def _best_effort_export(
    client: BoMcpClient,
    campaign_id: str,
    artifact_dir: Path,
) -> Path | None:
    try:
        content, content_type = client.export_campaign(campaign_id, fmt="csv")
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"Export skipped: {exc}")
        return None
    suffix = ".csv" if "csv" in content_type.lower() else ".bin"
    export_path = artifact_dir / f"campaign_export{suffix}"
    export_path.write_bytes(content)
    return export_path



def _finalize_campaign_state(
    client: BoMcpClient,
    campaign_id: str,
    *,
    terminate_on_exit: bool,
) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    campaign = client.get_campaign(campaign_id)
    status = campaign.get("status")
    if terminate_on_exit and status not in {"terminated"}:
        response = client.lifecycle(campaign_id, action="terminate")
        print(f"Terminated campaign {campaign_id}")
        return response
    if status == "running":
        response = client.lifecycle(campaign_id, action="pause")
        print(f"Paused campaign {campaign_id}")
        return response
    return None



def _write_manifest(manifest_path: Path, artifact_dir: Path) -> None:
    write_json(
        manifest_path,
        {
            "campaign_slug": CAMPAIGN_SLUG,
            "package_modules": [
                "ethanol_sds_contact_angle_65/__init__.py",
                "ethanol_sds_contact_angle_65/search_space.py",
                "ethanol_sds_contact_angle_65/intake.py",
                "ethanol_sds_contact_angle_65/evaluator.py",
                "ethanol_sds_contact_angle_65/reporting.py",
                "ethanol_sds_contact_angle_65/campaign.py",
            ],
            "run_entrypoint": "run_ethanol_sds_contact_angle_65.py",
            "latest_artifact_directory": str(artifact_dir),
        },
    )
"}

{"path":"HOW_TO_EXECUTE_CAMPAIGN.md","content":"# How to Execute the Ethanol + SDS BO/RAISE Campaign

## Files
- Entry point: `run_ethanol_sds_contact_angle_65.py`
- Package: `ethanol_sds_contact_angle_65/`
- Manifest: `campaign_manifest.json`

## What the script does
The script creates or resumes a BO-MCP campaign over:
- `Ethanol` in `0-60` v/v%
- `SDS` in `0-1` w/v%

It submits results for:
1. two curated warm-start experiments,
2. then up to two BO-suggested experiments,
3. with early stop if any measured `static_contact_angle` lands in `64-66` degrees.

The BO objective is a **match** objective targeting `65` degrees.

## Warm starts used
1. `Ethanol=0.0`, `SDS=0.60`
2. `Ethanol=15.0`, `SDS=0.35`

These were chosen to bracket the target region based on the reported SDS plateau and the observed ethanol-driven lowering of contact angle.

## Prerequisites
The script expects these environment variables to already be available:
- `BO_MCP_API_URL`
- `BO_MCP_API_KEY`

It runs through the repository's `uv` environment and uses the repository BO-MCP client plus the RAISE evaluator.

## Run a fresh campaign
```bash
uv run python run_ethanol_sds_contact_angle_65.py
```

## Resume an existing campaign
```bash
uv run python run_ethanol_sds_contact_angle_65.py --campaign-id <CAMPAIGN_ID>
```

## Run a bounded validation invocation
This keeps the campaign short and cleans it up afterward.
```bash
uv run python run_ethanol_sds_contact_angle_65.py \
  --warm-start-budget 2 \
  --bo-iteration-budget 1 \
  --terminate-on-exit
```

## Useful options
- Change the evaluator timeout:
```bash
uv run python run_ethanol_sds_contact_angle_65.py --raise-timeout-s 700
```

- Store artifacts somewhere else:
```bash
uv run python run_ethanol_sds_contact_angle_65.py --artifacts-root my_artifacts
```

## Artifacts to inspect after a run
Each invocation writes a new artifact directory under:
```text
artifacts/ethanol_sds_contact_angle_65/
```

Typical files include:
- `run_context.json`
- `evaluations.jsonl`
- `diagnostics.json` (best effort)
- `campaign_export.csv` (best effort)
- `run_summary.json`

The latest artifact directory is also recorded in `campaign_manifest.json`.

## How to validate the outcome
1. Read stdout for the campaign id, each submitted experiment, and the stop reason.
2. Check `run_summary.json` for the best observed angle and final campaign status.
3. Inspect `evaluations.jsonl` to see every warm-start and BO evaluation, including penalty fallbacks if RAISE fails.
4. Inspect `campaign_export.csv` for the BO-MCP campaign export.

## Notes on continuation behavior
- If the script is rerun with `--campaign-id`, it queries BO-MCP for existing results first.
- Existing warm-start results count toward the warm-start budget.
- Existing BO-submitted results count toward the BO-iteration budget.
- If a pending BO suggestion already exists, the script reuses it instead of generating a new one.
- If the campaign is paused, the script resumes it.
- If the campaign is completed, the script reopens it before continuing.

- RAISE may echo back submitted inputs with zero-valued parameters omitted (for example, it can omit `SDS: 0.0`). When `run_raise_experiment(...)` fails only because the echoed-input check rejects that omission, a script-level fallback can safely normalize the raw payload by treating missing expected zero-valued parameters as equivalent to the submitted candidate, while still rejecting unexpected extra keys or non-zero mismatches.
- For resumable BO loops, check BO for existing pending suggestions before generating a new suggestion. If a prior run paused after suggestion generation but before result submission, resuming against the pending suggestion avoids skipping or duplicating BO work.

- BO suggestion generation can return HTTP 200 with `success=false` when a campaign has hit `max_iterations`, `max_observations`, or other stopping criteria. In BO/RAISE runner scripts, do not treat that as an unexpected exception; detect the exhaustion envelope, print a concise completion message, and terminate/close the campaign cleanly instead of pausing on exception.

## BO/PySCF scripting caveats

- When submitting BO-MCP REST results to `POST /api/v1/results/{campaign_id}`, the `source` field must match the allowed pattern `^(gui|file_upload|api)$`; for agent-authored scripts, use `"api"` rather than a custom script name.

- When calling `run_pyscf_workflow` from a Python script via `uv run python`, the returned object is a `PySCFWorkflowResult` model (with fields such as `total_energy`, `workflow_summary`, and `pyscf_output.chkfile`), not a plain list; script code should read the energy from `result.total_energy`.

- BO-MCP categorical parameters require at least 2 categories each at campaign intake. For smoke tests of categorical campaigns, keep every categorical parameter at cardinality >= 2 and reduce budget/iterations instead of collapsing a parameter to a single category.
- When calling `run_pyscf_workflow` directly from Python, `result.analysis_results` may be a Pydantic model rather than a plain dict; use `model_dump()` before dict-style access like `.get(...)`.

- When extracting dipole data from `run_pyscf_workflow` molecular analysis in a direct Python script, `analysis_results.model_dump()["dipole_moment"]` can be a NumPy ndarray; convert via `.tolist()` or iterate and cast to float before computing the magnitude.

- In direct `uv run python` BO/PySCF scripts, `run_pyscf_workflow` is invoked synchronously (do **not** `await` it); it returns a `PySCFWorkflowResult` object directly.

- BO-MCP REST intake accepts a BayBE substance categorical parameter with `parameter_options={"baybe": {"role": "substance", "substance_data": {label: smiles}}}`; `substance_encoding` is optional, so agent-authored scripts can keep the intake minimal unless a specific encoding is required.

- BO-MCP `GET /api/v1/campaigns/{campaign_id}/export` may return a text/CSV payload rather than JSON; agent-authored REST scripts should inspect `Content-Type` and save the raw response body to an appropriate artifact file instead of assuming `response.json()` will work.

- To seed a fresh BO-MCP campaign from prior completed experiments, agent-authored REST scripts can submit historical observations directly to `POST /api/v1/results/{campaign_id}` using only `parameter_values`, `objective_values`, and optional `metadata`; `suggestion_id` is not required for these seed rows.

- BO-MCP REST campaign intake accepts lowercase neutral enums such as `{"type": "categorical"}` for input parameters and `{"direction": "maximize"}` for objectives; a minimal categorical intake with `backend="baybe"` validates cleanly via `POST /api/v1/campaigns/validate`.

- For resume-safe BO-MCP REST scripts, handle suggestion-generation read timeouts by listing pending suggestions on the campaign before generating a new batch and by polling for newly visible pending suggestions after a timeout; this avoids duplicating suggestion batches when the server created suggestions but the client timed out before reading the response.

- In direct workspace scripts that build MOFs through `domains.mofs.ontomofs` / PORMAKE inside this container.

- For PORMAKE-native categorical BO over `topology + node + edge` where node suitability depends on topology, a practical script pattern is to build the BO node category as the union of topology-specific node shortlists, then apply a topology-conditioned validity check inside the evaluator and submit finite penalty objectives for invalid topology/node combinations instead of crashing the campaign.

- For digital OSL campaign scripts that sanity-check `product_smiles.py` against `adk9227_data_s6.csv`, do not fail the run on a pure stereochemistry / canonical-SMILES representation mismatch when the generated product and backtest row have the same non-isomeric connectivity. Record the discrepancy in the backtest artifact and continue by default; reserve fail-fast behavior for hard connectivity mismatches (or an explicit strict-backtest mode).

- In direct workspace scripts that construct MOFs via `domains.mofs.ontomofs.MOFBuilder`, prefer `build_by_type(topology, node_bbs=..., edge_bbs=...)` over the simpler `build(topology, [..])` helper. On timeout, kill the worker process group, record the candidate as failed, reject the BO suggestion, and continue the campaign.

- For BO-MCP BayBE custom-categorical parameters, tiny smoke-test category sets can make some descriptor columns constant within a parameter. BayBE can reject such custom descriptor tables at campaign creation even if intake validation passes. A robust script pattern is to prune per-parameter descriptor columns that have only one unique value across the active categories, and if creation is still rejected, retry once with plain categorical parameters as a fallback.


- For BO-MCP BayBE custom-categorical parameters, every category label must have a unique descriptor vector at campaign creation time. In finite chemistry libraries, chemically distinct labels can share the same coarse RDKit descriptor tuple; a practical fix is to append deterministic fragment-identity codes (for example cap/core indices) to the compact descriptor table so BayBE can distinguish labels without abandoning the custom representation.

- In workspace Python scripts executed with `uv run python`, `from domains.raise_platform.tools import run_raise_experiment` is an async coroutine function. Call it with `asyncio.run(run_raise_experiment(...))` from synchronous scripts rather than treating it like a normal dict-returning function.

- For direct BO API result submission to `POST /api/v1/results/{campaign_id}`, the top-level `source` field must match the allowed pattern `gui|file_upload|api`. Use `"api"` for scripted submissions.
- When authoring BO campaign scripts that use BO API idempotency keys, make the campaign-creation key unique per logical run (for example, include a run nonce) rather than deriving it only from the intake payload. Otherwise rerunning the same named/spec-identical script can replay an earlier campaign creation response instead of creating a fresh campaign.

- In `uv run python` BO/RAISE scripts, `asyncio.run(run_raise_experiment(...))` can return a `RaiseExperimentResult` model object rather than a plain `dict`. Normalize it with `result.model_dump()` (or fall back to `result.input_parameters` / `result.static_contact_angle`) before subscripting.
